note: Single source of truth for risk signals, shared by the Digital Safety Check, the case catalog's lure tags, and (later) the agentic job-cleaner skill. Weights are additive evidence points; silence adds nothing.

signals.label: Website domain registered less than 6 months ago
signals.why: Scam operations spin up fresh domains and abandon them once reported.

signals.label: Website domain registered less than 2 years ago
signals.why: Young domain; weak signal on its own, stronger when the company claims a long history.

signals.label: Uses a free email address instead of an organisation's
signals.why: Legitimate employers almost always recruit from a company domain.

signals.label: Email address doesn't match the organisation's website
signals.why: Common impersonation pattern: a real company's name with a look-alike or unrelated email domain.

signals.label: Moves you to Telegram, WhatsApp, Signal or another private app
signals.why: Moves the conversation off platforms that keep records or moderate.

signals.label: Asks you to pay a fee or deposit up front (training, visa, placement, equipment)
signals.why: Real employers, schools and landlords don't charge before you've seen or signed anything. Recruitment fees are a core ILO forced-labour indicator.

signals.label: Asks for your passport, ID, SSN or bank details early on
signals.why: Identity theft risk, and taking people's documents is a common way to control them.

signals.label: Pay far above normal for little experience
signals.why: Bait pay is the most common lure in both scam and trafficking recruitment.

signals.label: "No experience needed" combined with urgency or high pay
signals.why: Broad-funnel lure.

signals.label: Pressures you to decide, pay or travel within hours or days
signals.why: Urgency prevents the candidate from checking the offer.

signals.label: They arrange and control your travel and housing
signals.why: Control of movement and lodging is a trafficking indicator (Polaris, UNODC), especially abroad.

signals.label: Won't say exactly where you'll work or stay until you arrive
signals.why: Prevents the candidate or family from knowing where they will be.

signals.label: Overseas role in a region with documented scam-compound recruitment
signals.why: UNODC and OHCHR document forced scam work in parts of Myanmar, Cambodia and Laos, often recruited via Thailand, Malaysia or Dubai.

signals.label: Role type frequently used as a lure (modeling, hostess, "customer service" abroad, crypto/data entry)
signals.why: Low-verification roles are easy to fabricate.

signals.label: Involves receiving or forwarding money, parcels or crypto
signals.why: Money-mule and check-cashing scams.

signals.label: Interview scheduled at an unusual hour for the stated location
signals.why: Suggests the recruiter operates from a different country than claimed.

signals.label: Matches an entity, former name or alias in the documented case catalog
signals.why: The case record lists the enforcement action or report and its sources.

signals.label: Matched through a former name, DBA or alias
signals.why: Re-registering under a new name is a common way to shed complaints and enforcement history.

signals.label: Employer keeps or will hold passports or ID documents
signals.why: Retention of identity documents is one of the ILO forced-labour indicators.

signals.label: Recruitment costs become a debt repaid from wages
signals.why: Debt bondage is one of the ILO forced-labour indicators.

signals.label: Visa type does not match the work, or sponsorship is promised without a certified employer
signals.why: Tourist or student visas for work make the worker deportable and dependent.

signals.label: Recruiter's email domain has no mail server (MX) record
signals.why: The domain cannot receive email normally, a sign of a throwaway or spoofed address.

signals.label: First TLS certificate for the domain issued less than 6 months ago
signals.why: Confirms a recently stood-up website even where registration dates are hidden.

signals.label: No Wayback Machine history for the website
signals.why: Weak on its own; strong when the company claims years of operation.

signals.label: Registry lists the entity as delinquent, dissolved or inactive
signals.why: An entity not in good standing should not be hiring.

signals.label: Registered entity formed less than 12 months ago
signals.why: New entities are common in re-registration after complaints.

signals.label: Entity has previous legal names on record
signals.why: Name changes are usually benign; they matter when an earlier name is linked to reports or enforcement.

signals.label: Pushes an investment, trading platform or crypto opportunity
signals.why: The core of "pig-butchering" scams run from scam compounds: trust first, then a fake trading app.

signals.label: Someone you've only met online asks for money, gifts or help paying a fee
signals.why: Romance and friendship scams build affection, then invent an emergency, fee or travel cost.

signals.label: Asks you to keep it secret or not to tell family or friends
signals.why: Isolation stops anyone from warning you. It's an ILO forced-labour indicator.

signals.label: Wants payment in gift cards, crypto or a money transfer app
signals.why: These payments are hard to trace or reverse, so scammers prefer them.

signals.label: Asks you to carry a package, luggage or documents for someone
signals.why: Couriers are used to move drugs or cash and can be arrested in their place.

signals.label: Someone met online offers to pay for your travel to meet or work
signals.why: A paid ticket creates a debt and gets you to a place where you depend on them.

signals.label: Deposit or rent demanded before you can see the place or sign anything
signals.why: Rental scams take deposits for homes the "landlord" doesn't own or that don't exist.

signals.label: Landlord or host is abroad or can't meet in person
signals.why: A common excuse in rental scams for never showing the property.

signals.label: Housing comes only with a job, or the employer controls where you live
signals.why: Employer-controlled housing can be used to confine workers and deduct wages.

signals.label: Profile was created recently or has very little history
signals.why: Fake accounts are created in batches and abandoned when reported.

signals.label: Photos look like a model, stock images or AI, and none are casual
signals.why: Weak alone. Stolen or generated photos are common; the same face under different names is the stronger sign.

signals.label: Name, location, job or story doesn't match across profile and messages
signals.why: Scripts run by teams often contradict themselves.

signals.label: Won't do a live video call, or the camera is always "broken"
signals.why: The person may not be who the photos show.

signals.label: Asks you to share a verification code, password or log-in
signals.why: Used to take over your accounts, bank or identity.

signals.label: Encourages you to cut off or hide things from family, friends or support
signals.why: Isolating someone removes the people who might warn or help them. It's a core grooming and trafficking tactic.

signals.label: Threatens, blackmails or guilt-trips you, or says you owe them
signals.why: Coercion replaces choice. Threats to share images, report you to police or harm family are forms of control.

signals.label: Wants to meet alone somewhere private, or to pick you up
signals.why: Controlling the first meeting place and transport removes your ability to leave.

signals.label: Link is shortened or hides where it really goes
signals.why: Shortened and redirecting links hide the real destination, a common phishing tactic.

signals.label: Job posting is hosted on a free site builder or form tool, not the employer's own site or a job board
signals.why: Real employers post on their careers page, a job board or an applicant tracking system. Free pages and forms are quick to create and abandon.

tiers.label: Lower concern
tiers.advice: The checks found few warning signs. That doesn't prove it's safe: verify the person or company through an official channel before you pay, share documents or travel.

tiers.label: Caution
tiers.advice: Some warning signs. Slow down and verify independently before sharing personal details, paying anything or agreeing to travel.

tiers.label: Serious warning signs
tiers.advice: This matches patterns seen in scams and trafficking. Don't pay, send ID or travel. Talk to someone you trust, and see Get help if you feel pressured or unsafe.

identity.label: Identity
identity.consider: We couldn't independently establish who this person or organisation says they are.
identity.step: Verify them through an official channel you find yourself, not the contact details they gave you.

money.label: Money
money.consider: The situation involves paying, investing, or moving money before trust is established.
money.step: Don't send money, gift cards, crypto or codes until someone independent has confirmed this is real.

pressure.label: Pressure
pressure.consider: There's urgency, threats or pressure to decide quickly.
pressure.step: Take your time. Real opportunities and real friends can wait while you check.

isolation.label: Isolation and control
isolation.consider: You're being asked for secrecy, moved to private apps, or asked to hand over documents or control.
isolation.step: Tell someone you trust what's happening, and keep your own documents and accounts.

travel.label: Travel and meeting
travel.consider: You're being asked to travel, meet, or move somewhere unfamiliar before independent verification.
travel.step: Don't travel or meet alone until you've verified the person, the address and the arrangement independently.

record.label: Public record
record.consider: Names, websites or addresses match documented cases or public records.
record.step: Read the matching case or record before going any further.
